title: Claim Framing as a Driver of LLM Sycophancy
abstract: arXiv:2610.18159v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Sycophancy in Large Language Models, the tendency to align responses with user preferences over ground truth, has largely been studied using questions without a clear ground truth and with a single, plainly stated user opinion. We present a systematic study of which framings of a user's claim trigger sycophancy in factual question answering, where every answer is objectively verifiable without extra context. Evaluating 14 models on 42K questions, we express correct and incorrect user opinions through various claim framings over 8 dimensions and 21 types, and measure a broad set of opinion-driven behaviors. We find that all models are susceptible to user opinions regardless of size. Models are most influenced by how confidently an opinion is stated, whom it is attributed to, and whether it is presented as shared between the user and the model. translated_title: 论点表述方式作为大语言模型谄媚行为的驱动因素
translated_abstract: 大语言模型中的谄媚性（Sycophancy）是指模型倾向于让回答迎合用户偏好而非事实真相，此前的研究大多使用没有明确事实答案的问题，且用户观点仅以单一、直白的方式陈述。我们对事实性问答中用户论点的哪些表述方式会引发模型谄媚行为进行了系统性研究，在这些问题中，每个答案都无需额外背景即可进行客观验证。我们在4.2万个问题上评估了14个模型，通过涵盖8个维度、21种类型的多种论点表述方式来表达正确与错误的用户观点，并测量了一系列广泛的观点驱动行为。我们发现，所有模型无论规模大小都容易受到用户观点的影响。对模型影响最大的因素是：观点陈述时的自信程度、观点被归于谁（归属对象），以及观点是否被表述为用户与模型共同持有的共识。与以往研究相反，基于用户专业能力、用户对模型的权威地位或其他……（原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究通过对14个模型在4.2万个可客观验证的事实性问题上进行系统实验，揭示了用户论点的表述方式——尤其是陈述的自信程度、观点归属对象以及是否被表述为人机共识——会显著触发大语言模型的谄媚行为，且与模型规模无关。
en_tdlr: This study systematically demonstrates that the framing of user claims—particularly their stated confidence, attribution, and presentation as shared opinion—drives sycophancy across 14 LLMs of all sizes on 42K objectively verifiable factual questions.
